sections.content:
Population change in Birmingham in 2032

The population in Birmingham is projected to increase from 1,154,221 people in 2022 to 1,191,154 people in 2032.

Despite an overall increase in the population, there is projected to be a fall in net internal migration, which will decrease the population by 146,761 people.

This will also be the biggest factor in population change in most areas in England.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Birmingham
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Birmingham, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More births than deaths mean that the population is projected to increase by 52,266, with 143,290 births and 91,024 deaths in Birmingham between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would increase the population in Birmingham by 4.5%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to reduce the population by 146,761, with 591,039 people moving to the area and 737,800 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Birmingham by 12.7%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 4,046, with 22,817 people moving to the area and 26,863 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Birmingham by 0.4%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 136,486, with 235,989 people moving to the area and 99,503 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Birmingham by 11.8%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Birmingham in 2032

The median age in Birmingham is projected to rise from 34 years in 2022 to 35 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 13% of the population in Birmingham are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 12% in 2022.

sections.title: The 20 to 29 age group are set to see the largest change in Birmingham between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Birmingham is projected to stay the same, at around 68%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to fall from 188 to 182 over the same time period.

This is below average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Birmingham?

In 2032, 23% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 26% in 2022.

This is above average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Birmingham between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will stay around the same, at 6%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 10% to 8%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will fall from 10% to 9%
